gate1.edge_statement: We apply our capital structure expertise to evaluate the recovery value of Chrysler Financial debt claims during a government-mandated restructuring.

gate2.variant_view: The market is pricing Chrysler Financial debt based on extreme systemic contagion fears and pessimistic recovery assumptions regarding government-led restructuring. We believe the discrete nature of the asset-backed SPV structure and the government's vested interest in maintaining liquidity for automotive dealers ensures a higher recovery value for creditors than the current distressed pricing reflects. The catalyst for value realization will be the orderly unwinding of the loan book under the government-monitored restructuring framework.

final.memo:
We are initiating a position in the distressed debt of Chrysler Financial, a business the market has incorrectly grouped with the systemic failure of the parent automaker [D01, D06]. While the parent company faces profound existential challenges, Chrysler Financial operates as a distinct legal entity with an isolated SPV structure that houses the underlying retail auto loan book [D01, D04]. The market has sold these credits down to distressed levels, failing to account for the structural protections of the SPV and the vital role of these assets in maintaining dealer liquidity [D03, D05].

Our analysis suggests a recovery value for these credit claims of 70-80 cents on the dollar, a significant premium to current trading levels [D05, D06]. We base this on the collateralization of the retail loan book and the safety net provided by the $1.5bn government-backed facility [D01, D03, D04]. By benchmarking against historical consumer default curves for similar asset-backed finance vehicles, we believe the downside risk is mitigated at a floor of 50-60 cents on the dollar, providing an attractive risk-reward profile [D05, D06].

The mispricing stems from a failure to distinguish between parent-level equity volatility and the specific legal seniority afforded to SPV creditors [D05, D06]. We intend to engage as a constructive participant in the restructuring process to ensure the absolute priority rule is strictly upheld [D03, D07]. Our goal is to prevent any court-mandated intercompany transfers that would dilute the value of these secured claims [D04, D06].

Our plan is to retain local counsel to represent our interests on the creditor committee, ensuring that the U.S. Treasury—which is the primary driver of the restructuring—maintains the integrity of the SPV framework [D03, D07]. We expect the resolution of this situation to take approximately four quarters [D03, D04]. We are sizing this position at 3% of NAV, reflecting our high conviction in the legal structure despite the broader volatility in the financial sector, and we are hedging this exposure with a CDS overlay on a broader financial index to neutralize systemic contagion risks [D01, D05].
